task.speaker: client
task.text:
Hi Kenji,

This is exactly the study I had hoped to see. Isolating height finally let me evaluate the image I had in mind, so thank you for working through it with me.

Please adopt the 2% increase as our new baseline. For the Hero V, it creates the right degree of quiet elevation without becoming overstated.

Before proceeding, though, several previously established design rules appear to have been unintentionally unlocked and need to be restored:

1\. Treat the É accent as an exact copy of the Hero V’s right-arm terminal.

It must not be interpreted independently. The Hero V remains the master geometry, and the accent should inherit that form exactly.

2\. Align the É accent’s peak at precisely the same height as the Hero V’s right arm.

That exact relationship is now an important part of the visual language.

3\. Keep the second V significantly more restrained.

It should carry the same design language, but quietly. Calculate its percentage increase from the second V’s original height rather than trying to match the Hero V visually. Its right arm should rise proportionally above the alphabet while remaining almost imperceptible. The current version is too expressive: the second V must echo the Hero V, never compete with it.

For the next comparison, please add three reference lines: the current guide that shows the calibrated increase from the original baseline, a guide through the Hero V right-arm peak to verify perfect alignment with the É accent, and a guide at the rest of the alphabet’s cap height so we can refine exactly how far the second V rises above it.

We’re no longer looking for new concepts. The work now concerns the relationships among the three signature elements that define the identity—details people may not consciously notice but will instinctively recognize.

Thank you again. I genuinely feel we’re very close.
